newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aldeasa may be privatised in spring 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aldeasa may be privatised in spring 1997.

text.p: Spanish duty-free shop manager Aldeasa may be privatised next spring, chairman Jose Fernandez Olano said on Monday.
He estimated that the firm's profits through to 1999 will total at least 20 billion pesetas.
"The privatisation will go ahead, perhaps this spring," he told journalists.
The firm's licence to operate duty-free shops in Spanish airports has been renewed by its second largest shareholder, Aeropuertos Espanoles (AENA), Fernandez said.
The Spanish state owns 80 percent of the company and AENA owns the other 20 percent.
The renewal of the licence, valid for 10 years, will allow the company's value to increase ahead of its flotation, he said.
However Fernandez said the percentage of Aldeasa to be offered on the stock market has not been decided.
Aldeasa posted a pretax profit of 6.47 billion pesetas in the nine months to end-September, up 20.1 percent year on year. Sales rose 23.2 percent o 37.37 billion pesetas.
Fernandez forecast that pretax profit for 1996 will total around 8.2 - 8.2 billion pesetas, and turnover will increase to 50 billion pesetas.
